title: Is The Million-Token Context Window A Lie? The Honest Verdict
description:
Every model on the market sells you a million-token context window, and the top comment is always the same: so the real window is 4k? Here's the honest verdict. The number isn't a lie. It's just the wrong number to trust.
 
A million is the input limit: how much text you're allowed to paste in. The number nobody prints is the comprehension limit: how much the model still gets right. Run the needle-in-a-haystack test and that second number shows up. Accuracy holds clean up to about 32K tokens. Push past it and the model starts quietly skimming instead of reading.
 
Gemini sells 2M. GPT sells 400K. Same cliff. The causes differ from model to model (sliding-window truncation, the attention sink, the lost middle), but the wall lands in roughly the same place.
 
So budget against 32K, not the number on the box. Treat the million like the size of the fuel tank, and 32K like how far it actually drives.
 
The window is real. The attention is the part they don't sell you.
